cues.zh: 那我们这期就做机器人三定律的视频，怎么样？
cues.en: So, should we do a video about the three laws of robotics, then?

cues.zh: 因为评论区老是提到它。
cues.en: Because it keeps coming up in the comments.

cues.zh: 好吧，问题是，你不会听到严肃的AI研究者谈论机器人三定律
cues.en: Okay, so the thing is, you won't hear serious AI researchers talking about the three laws of robotics

cues.zh: 因为它们行不通。它们从来就没行通过。
cues.en: because they don't work. They never worked.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得大家看不到有人讨论三定律，是因为它们不严肃。
cues.en: So I think people don't see the three laws talked about, because they're not serious.

cues.zh: 它们已经很久很久都不相关了，而且它们还是出自一本科幻小说，你懂的？
cues.en: They haven't been relevant for a very long time and they're out of a science fiction book, you know?

cues.zh: 所以，我来做吧。我想说清楚，我并不把这些当回事，对吧？
cues.en: So, I'm going to do it. I want to be clear that I'm not taking these seriously, right?

cues.zh: 但我还是要讲一讲，因为这事需要被讨论。
cues.en: I'm going to talk about it anyway, because it needs to be talked about.

cues.zh: 这些是科幻作家Isaac Asimov在他的故事里提出的一些规则，
cues.en: So these are some rules that science fiction author Isaac Asimov came up with, in his stories,

cues.zh: 试图作为一种解决方案，来确保人工智能做
cues.en: as an attempted sort of solution to the problem of making sure that artificial intelligence did

cues.zh: 我们想让它做的事。
cues.en: what we want it to do.

cues.zh: 那我们念出来看看是什么？
cues.en: Shall we read them out then and see what they are?

cues.zh: 好啊，我看看——稍等一下。
cues.en: Oh yeah, I'll look them- Give me a second.

cues.zh: 我查到了。好，是这样的：
cues.en: I've looked them up. Okay, right, so they are:

cues.zh: 第一定律：机器人不得伤害人类，也不得因不作为而使人类
cues.en: Law Number 1: A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction allow a human being

cues.zh: 受到伤害。
cues.en: to come to harm.

cues.zh: 第二定律：机器人必须服从人类的命令，除非该命令
cues.en: Law Number 2: A robot must obey orders given it by human beings except where such orders would

cues.zh: 与第一定律冲突。
cues.en: conflict with the first law.

cues.zh: 第三定律：机器人必须保护自身的存在，只要这种保护不与
cues.en: Law Number 3: A robot must protect its own existence as long as such protection does not conflict

cues.zh: 第一或第二定律冲突。
cues.en: with the first or second laws.

cues.zh: 我记得后来还有个第零定律。
cues.en: I think there was a zeroth one later as well.

cues.zh: 第零定律：机器人不得伤害人类整体，也不得因不作为而使人类整体受到伤害。
cues.en: Law 0: A robot may not harm humanity or, by inaction, allow humanity to come to harm.

cues.zh: 这些老是出现挺奇怪的，因为，首先它们是某个
cues.en: So it's weird that these keep coming up because, okay, so firstly they were made by someone

cues.zh: 写故事的人编出来的，对吧？而且是为写故事而优化的。
cues.en: who is writing stories, right? And they're optimized for story-writing.

cues.zh: 但它们在书里根本行不通，对吧？如果你读过那些书，它们讲的都是
cues.en: But they don't even work in the books, right? If you read the books, they're all about

cues.zh: 这些规则出错的方式，各种各样、形形色色的负面后果。
cues.en: the ways that these rules go wrong, the various, various negative consequences.

cues.zh: 在我看来，阿西莫夫处理这些设定最不真实的地方在于
cues.en: The most unrealistic thing, in my opinion, about the way Asimov did his stuff was

cues.zh: 事情出错然后又得到修复的方式，对吧？
cues.en: the way that things go wrong and then get fixed, right?

cues.zh: 大多数时候，如果你有一个超级智能，它在做你不想让它做的事，
cues.en: Most of the time, if you have a super-intelligence, that is doing something you don't want it to do,

cues.zh: 大概不会有英雄靠聪明才智来拯救局面。现实生活不是那样运作的，
cues.en: there's probably no hero who's going to save the day with cleverness. Real life doesn't work that way,

cues.zh: 一般来说，对吧？因为它们是用英语写的。你怎么定义这些东西？
cues.en: generally speaking, right? Because they're written in English. How do you define these things?

cues.zh: 你怎么定义“人类”，而不必先几乎在每个问题上都采取伦理立场？
cues.en: How do you define human without having to first take an ethical stand on almost every issue?

cues.zh: 如果“人类”还不够难，你还得定义“伤害”，对吧？
cues.en: And if human wasn't hard enough, you then have to define harm, right?

cues.zh: 你又遇到了同样的问题。几乎你给这些词下的任何定义，
cues.en: And you've got the same problem again. Almost any definitions you give for those words,

cues.zh: 那些真正扎实、明确、不依赖人类直觉的定义，
cues.en: really solid, unambiguous definitions that don't rely on human intuition,

cues.zh: 都会导致哲学上的奇怪怪癖，结果让你的 AI 做出你根本不想让它做的事。
cues.en: result in weird quirks of philosophy, resulting in your AI doing something you really don't want it to do.

cues.zh: 问题是，为了编码那条规则——“不允许人类受到伤害”，
cues.en: The thing is, in order to encode that rule, "Don't allow a human being to come to harm",

cues.zh: 并且让它表达的意思接近我们直觉上理解的含义，
cues.en: in a way that means anything close to what we intuitively understand it to mean,

cues.zh: 你就得在“人类”和“伤害”这两个词里编码整个伦理学领域，对吧？
cues.en: you would have to encode within the words 'human' and 'harm' the entire field of ethics, right?

cues.zh: 你必须全面解决伦理学问题，然后用它来制定你的定义。
cues.en: You have to solve ethics, comprehensively, and then use that to make your definitions.

cues.zh: 所以这并没有解决问题，只是把问题往回推了一步，
cues.en: So it doesn't solve the problem, it pushes the problem back one step

cues.zh: 变成：好吧，我们怎么定义这些术语？
cues.en: into now, well how do we define these terms?

cues.zh: 当我说“人类”这个词时，你知道我指的是什么，这并不是因为我们俩
cues.en: When I say the word human, you know what I mean, and that's not because either of us

cues.zh: 对人类是什么有严格的定义。我们只是通过一般的联想
cues.en: have a rigorous definition of what a human is. We've just sort of learned by general association

cues.zh: 学到了人类是什么，然后“人类”这个词指向你大脑中的那个结构，
cues.en: what a human is, and then the word 'human' points to that structure in your brain,

cues.zh: 但我并没有真正把内容传递给你。
cues.en: but I'm not really transferring the content to you.

cues.zh: 所以，你不能只是在AI的效用函数里写上“人类”就指望它知道那是什么意思。
cues.en: So, you can't just say 'human' in the utility function of an AI and have it know what that means.

cues.zh: 你必须明确指定。你必须给出一个定义。
cues.en: You have to specify. You have to come up with a definition.

cues.zh: 而事实证明，要为“人类”这样的东西给出一个定义，一个好的定义，
cues.en: And it turns out that coming up with a definition, a good definition, of something like 'human'

cues.zh: 是极其困难的，对吧？这本质上是一个道德哲学的难题。
cues.en: is extremely difficult, right? It's a really hard problem of, essentially, moral philosophy.

cues.zh: 你可能会以为这是语义学问题，但其实并不是，因为，
cues.en: You would think it would be semantics, but it really isn't because,

cues.zh: 好吧，我们可以同意我是人类，你也是人类。这没问题。
cues.en: okay, so we can agree that I'm a human and you're a human. That's fine.

cues.zh: 比如这是一张桌子，因此不是人。
cues.en: And that this, for example, is a table, and therefore not a human.

cues.zh: 你看，简单的部分，各类别的核心例子都很明显。
cues.en: You know, the easy stuff, the central examples of the classes are obvious.

cues.zh: 但边界情况，也就是类别的边缘，变得非常重要。
cues.en: But, the edge cases, the boundaries of the classes, become really important.

cues.zh: 也就是我们不确定究竟什么才算人的那些区域。
cues.en: The areas in which we're not sure exactly what counts as a human.

cues.zh: 比如，还没出生的人，抽象地说，就是假设
cues.en: So, for example, people who haven't been born yet, in the abstract, like people who hypothetically

cues.zh: 可能十年后才会出生的人，他们算吗？
cues.en: could be born ten years in the future, do they count?

cues.zh: 处于持续性植物状态的人没有任何大脑活动。
cues.en: People who are in a persistent vegetative state don't have any brain activity.

cues.zh: 他们完全算作人吗？已经去世的人，或者未出生的胎儿，对吧？
cues.en: Do they fully count as people? People who have died or unborn fetuses, right?

cues.zh: 我是说，就在我们说话的当下，关于他们是否算作人，还有一场巨大的争论。
cues.en: I mean, there's a huge debate even going on as we speak about whether they count as people.

cues.zh: 高等动物，你知道，我们该不该把海豚、黑猩猩之类的算进来？
cues.en: The higher animals, you know, should we include maybe dolphins, chimpanzees, something like that?

cues.zh: 它们有重量吗？结果发现，你没法编程，你没法制定你的规范
cues.en: Do they have weight? And so it it turns out you can't program in, you can't make your specification

cues.zh: 关于人类，而不对所有这些议题采取伦理立场。
cues.en: of humans without taking an ethical stance on all of these issues.

cues.zh: 各种奇怪、假设性的边缘情况都会变得相关，当你在谈论
cues.en: All kinds of weird, hypothetical edge cases become relevant when you're talking about

cues.zh: 一个非常强大的机器智能时，这些情况你本来根本不会想到。
cues.en: a very powerful machine intelligence, which you otherwise wouldn't think of.

cues.zh: 比如，假设我们说死人不再算作人类。
cues.en: So for example, let's say we say that dead people don't count as humans.

cues.zh: 那么你就会有一个人工智能，它永远不会尝试心肺复苏。这个人已经死了。
cues.en: Then you have an AI which will never attempt CPR. This person's died.

cues.zh: 他们没了，别管了，结束了，对吧？
cues.en: They're gone, forget about it, done, right?

cues.zh: 而我们会说，不，等一下，他们只是暂时死了。我们可以把他们救回来，对吧？
cues.en: Whereas we would say, no, hang on a second, they're only dead temporarily. We can bring them back, right?

cues.zh: 好吧，行，那我们就说死去的人，如果他们还没死——嗯，多久算？
cues.en: Okay, fine, so then we'll say that people who are dead, if they haven't been dead for- Well, how long?

cues.zh: 你得死多久才算死？我是说，如果你搞错了，随口说一句“哦，没事”，
cues.en: How long do you have to be dead for? I mean, if you get that wrong and you just say, oh it's fine,

cues.zh: 试着把死人救活，那你可能造出一台机器，
cues.en: do try to bring people back once they're dead, then you may end up with a machine

cues.zh: 拼命想复活历史上所有死过的人，
cues.en: that's desperately trying to revive everyone who's ever died in all of history,

cues.zh: 因为有些人算数，有道德分量。
cues.en: because there are people who count who have moral weight.

cues.zh: 我们想要这样吗？我不知道，也许吧。但你得做决定，对吧？
cues.en: Do we want that? I don't know, maybe. But you've got to decide, right?

cues.zh: 而这本身就内嵌在你对“人”的定义里。你必须在各种道德问题上表态，
cues.en: And that's inherent in your definition of human. You have to take a stance on all kinds of moral issues

cues.zh: 而我们其实并没有把握答案是什么，只是为了把程序写进去。
cues.en: that we don't actually know with confidence what the answer is, just to program the thing in.

cues.zh: 然后比这还难，因为有些边缘情况现在根本不存在。
cues.en: And then it gets even harder than that, because there are edge cases which don't exist right now.

cues.zh: 比如，讨论活人、死人、未出生的人，诸如此类。
cues.en: Like, talking about living people, dead people, unborn people, that kind of thing.

cues.zh: 好吧，动物们。但存在各种各样可能存在的假想事物
cues.en: Fine, animals. But there are all kinds of hypothetical things which could exist

cues.zh: 它们算不算人类，还不好说。比如，模拟或仿真的大脑，对吧？
cues.en: which may or may not count as human. For example, emulated or simulated brains, right?

cues.zh: 如果你非常精确地扫描了某人的大脑，然后运行那个模拟，那算是一个人吗？
cues.en: If you have a very accurate scan of someone's brain and you run that simulation, is that a person?

cues.zh: 那算数吗？
cues.en: Does that count?

cues.zh: 无论你怎么切分这个问题，都会得到有趣的结果。
cues.en: And whichever way you slice that, you get interesting outcomes.

cues.zh: 所以，如果那算作一个人，那么你的机器可能会倾向于营造一种情境
cues.en: So, if that counts as a person, then your machine might be motivated to bring out a situation

cues.zh: 其中不存在物理人类，因为物理人类很难供养。
cues.en: in which there are no physical humans because physical humans are very difficult to provide for.

cues.zh: 而模拟人类，你可以模拟他们的输入，为每个人提供更好的环境。
cues.en: Whereas simulated humans, you can simulate their inputs and have a much nicer environment for everyone.

cues.zh: 那是我们想要的吗？我不知道。也许是？我不知道。
cues.en: Is that what we want? I don't know. Is it, maybe? I don't know.

cues.zh: 我觉得没人知道。但重点是，你在这里是想写一个 AI，对吧？
cues.en: I don't think anybody does. But the point is, you're trying to write an AI here, right?

cues.zh: 你是 AI 开发者。这可不是你当初报名要干的事。
cues.en: You're an AI developer. You didn't sign up for this.
